correctness.rationale: The projective-plane axioms give exact distance shells and B B^T=qI+J. A four-sector powered-distance eigendecomposition explicitly accounts for all dimensions. The color-antisymmetric branch is strictly negative and the only critical branch crosses zero once, giving the unique root. Its (v-1)-dimensional kernel consists exactly of (-By/sqrt(q),y) for centered y; Schoenberg Gram rank yields endpoint dimension v. Strict monotonicity and implicit-function expansion prove the remaining assertions. The packaged standard-library checker separately verifies all distances and integer incidence identities for orders 2,3,4,5,7, and validates finite root/equality examples; these experiments are not used as the infinite-order proof.

originality.rationale: Directly inspected primary finite-metric negative-type and graph-roundness literature supplies general criteria, but not the exact projective-plane order law, complete endpoint equality subspace, sparse two-line equality, or sharp critical snowflake ranks. Targeted record searches returned nearby projective-incidence homology/topology, ordinary adjacency spectra, and different graph-metric generalized-roundness claims rather than an equivalent or stronger statement. There remains unindexed-publication risk, especially because the matrix method is elementary once one knows the incidence identities.

value.rationale: A natural infinite diameter-three design family receives a complete sharp negative-type threshold, equality-subspace classification, and a precise critical Hilbert dimension drop from 2v-1 to v; the two-line equality gives a geometric finite-support certificate, while asymptotic q^{-1/2} degradation identifies a meaningful large-order trend.
